--- Log opened Sat Dec 07 00:00:57 2002
00:21 < jal0> so, antagonizt whacha working on?

00:35 < antagonizt> sort of
00:35 < jal0> cool, just finished mapping out the nand chip
00:36 < jal0> going to map a little more, then update my docs
00:37 < antagonizt> neat, anything that will help us write a NAND driver?
00:37 < jal0> btw, i leaning toward the unknow being some ASIC chip
00:37 < jal0> eventually, yeap
00:38 < antagonizt> ASIC? async IC?
00:38 < jal0> nope, check the NEC website, their custom chips, similar to dsp i guess you could say
00:39 < jal0> their built with macro functions which ARE documented
00:39 < antagonizt> cool
01:25 < jal0> antagonizt: do you remember what CN3 ( http://www.linux4.be/~jal0/top_bot_HIRES.jpg ) was connected to?
01:36 < antagonizt> the lcd?
01:36 < antagonizt> not sure
01:37 < jal0> ok, i'll ask filip later
01:38 < antagonizt> from the russian pics it looks like it was connected to CN1 on the LCD board
01:38 < antagonizt> http://www.linux4.be/~jroark/images/LCD_bot.jpg
01:38 < antagonizt> http://www.linux4.be/~jroark/images/Board_bot.jpg
01:39 < jal0> can tell for sure, cn3 on the mainboard bottom
01:39 < jal0> can=cant
01:39 < antagonizt> do you have a be around?
01:40 < jal0> yeah, but not apart
02:28 < jal0> antagonizt: still awake ?
02:28 < jal0> just updated my page with the new data
02:32 < antagonizt> cool i'll check it out
02:35 < antagonizt> is this something casio could get upset about?
02:35 < jal0> dont think so
02:35 < antagonizt> what with the dmca and all...
02:36 < jal0> dmca?
02:37 < antagonizt> digital millenium copyright act
02:37 < antagonizt> notorious for it's use to stop RE projects
02:38 < jal0> nah, at least in the USA, reverse engineering a product for personal use, so long as you own it, is not illegal, it falls under the 'Fair Use' clause of the copyright laws
02:40 < jal0> besides, as you can see, to completly RE this thing would take for ever, we just need to do enough for we can get basic fuctionaliy going. The rest we can do with software snooping
02:41 < antagonizt> well then i guess i should stop production of all those BE clones i've been working so hard on... :)
02:41 < jal0> hehe :-)
02:41 < jal0> me too
02:42 < jal0> so any luck so far with your driver?
02:43 < antagonizt> baahhh... can't the timer and wait queue funcs to do what i think they should...
02:43 < antagonizt> can't get
02:44 < antagonizt> if i knew the irq the buttons used it would be pretty simple
02:45 < jal0> have you looked at the vr4131 manual... i believe there are only 3 external irq lines on the chip, just wipe out the vectors for them.
02:48 < jal0> what do you mean by irq?
02:48 < antagonizt> the interrupt generated by pressing the button
02:48 < antagonizt> s
02:49 < antagonizt> i'm not sure i understand the hardware aspect of it all
02:49 < jal0> yeah, but what are you looking for?
02:49 < antagonizt> a number
02:49 < antagonizt> that i plug into the request_irq function :)
02:51 < jal0> i dont think the irq code works at all, your probably going to have to do it the hard way, by finding the interrupt mask register bit which coorisponds to the irq line(irq0,irq1,irq2) for external devices.
02:52 < jal0> this has nothing to do with the kernel because the irq code does not work in the kernel
02:52 < antagonizt> i thought all the vr4131 processor specific code was already written?
02:53 < antagonizt> you think it's broken?
02:53 < jal0> at least with the irq stuff specifice to the be300, yes, but broken is not the word, it just has to be initialized properly
02:54 < antagonizt> hmmm i guess i need to do some reading
02:55 < jal0> due to the fact that buttons are external devices, the stock vr4131 has no way of knowing how to handle them, you have to configure it specific to the device in which it's being used
02:57 < jal0> i believe the functionaliy it there, it just has to be set up
03:01 < antagonizt> hmmm i thought all available irq lines were auto magically set up...
03:03 < jal0> maybe internal once, but not external, how would they know where the external device was located on the bus?
03:03 < jal0> once=ones
03:04 < antagonizt> GPIO stands for general purpose input output right?
03:04 < jal0> yeap
03:05 < antagonizt> wouldn't external devices use the PGIO interrupts?
03:05 < antagonizt> GIO rather
03:05 < antagonizt> gpio
03:05 < jal0> when an irq is signaled, the cpu looks up the vector for a handling function. This handling function purpose is to query external devices to determin if they were the source of the interrupt. in order for this to happen the address of the external device has to be known
03:06 < antagonizt> i thought that is what the request_irq function does? 
03:06 < jal0> GPIO are just that general pupose input/output, not irq lines
03:07 < antagonizt> there are 32 GPIO irqs defined in include/asm/vr4122/vr4122.h
03:08 < jal0> i'll have to look at the irq code in the kernel, i havn't got much experience with linux kernal hacking.
03:08 < jal0> hang on let me take a look at something
03:13 < jal0> ugg, going to take more that a couple of minutes to digest the irq code in the kernel.
03:14 < antagonizt> yeah it's pretty complex
03:14 < jal0> btw, have you checked out 0xAF000080 -> 0xAF0000BA, that should be were all the ICU registers are located.
03:15 < antagonizt> i haven't...
03:15 < antagonizt> ICU = interrupt control unit?
03:15 < jal0> yeah
03:16 -!- metalac [~dejann@12-228-100-37.client.attbi.com] has joined #linux4be
03:16 < jal0> what connector is used to connect the keys to the main board? i'll start mapping out the i/o lines for them.
03:17 < antagonizt> so many three letter acronyms... hard to keep track of
03:17 < jal0> :)
03:17 < antagonizt> not sure... one of the smaller ones i imagine...
03:18 < antagonizt> i fi had to guess i would say CN1

03:19 < metalac> it's 12:19 here :)
03:20 < metalac> i'm assuming english language doesn't have a greeting for this time of day/night, since nobody is supposed to be greeting anyone at this hour, people are expected to be asleep :)
03:21 < jal0> hmm, never though about it, but no, no word that i can think of
03:22 < metalac> i mean they always teach you those basic 3 nothing more
03:22 < metalac> maybe a slang here and there, but nothing past 9:00 :)
03:26 < jal0> i would say ... morning(12:01AM->11:59)... afternoon(12:00PM->dusk) .... evening(dusk->sunset) .... night(sunset->11:59PM) ... :)
03:27 < jal0> so for antagonizt and me it would be 'morning'
03:27 < metalac> but good night is more of a departing saying, rather than the one you say when you meet someone
03:28 < jal0> thats good-buy ;)
03:29 < jal0> but in greetings, use 'evening' in place of night

03:32 < jal0> antagonizt: http://www.linux.org/docs/ldp/howto/KernelAnalysis-HOWTO-12.html
03:35 < antagonizt> thanks
03:35 < jal0> not much there though :)
03:48 < antagonizt> does that "article" suggest that there is a general function that is called on every interrupt which in turn calls a function, if any, that is associated with that irq?
03:49 < jal0> yeap
03:49 < antagonizt> so shouldn't i be able to add a printk inside that general func that spits out the irq # for all unhandled irqs
03:49 < antagonizt> ?
03:49 < jal0> handles housekeeping stuff like updating the timer and stuff
03:49 < antagonizt> so i can find the button irq this way... no?
03:50 < jal0> probably can stick a printk there, but not sure if it can tell you all the irq numbers, but then again it never hurts to try
03:51 < jal0>  heres another good reference -> http://www.xml.com/ldd/chapter/book/pdf/ch09.pdf
03:52 < antagonizt> yeah i have that book it's very usefull
03:54 < jal0> is there any way to access /proc/interrupts ?
03:54 < jal0> or has that even been setup in our kernel?

20:31 -!- nykkto [~nykkto@ns2.onkelinx.com] has quit [Remote closed the connection]
21:05 < antagonizt> hmmm... jal0 did you ever work on the serial driver?
21:05 < jal0> not yet wanted to map some of the addr/data lines first
21:06 < jal0> why
21:06 < antagonizt> i was looking at some of the interrupt code and found the interrupt i was using (found it in the RE CE code) is defined as a software interrupt
21:06 < antagonizt> #define VR4122_IRQ_SOFT      19
21:06 < jal0> irq you were using in the serial driver?
21:07 < antagonizt> trying to use... it never worked
21:09 < jal0> i dont think all of the register address for the serial driver are correct, so setting the IMR will not have the effect expected. have you looked at my lastest updates? it may help to explain why
21:09 < antagonizt> update to what?
21:10 < jal0> be300 schematic
21:10 < jal0> the address lines and how they are connected to the unknown chip
21:11 < antagonizt> what should i be looking for?
21:11 < jal0> btw, if you want an into what an ASIC chip is about --> http://www.nec.de/_PDF/13821e10.pdf
21:11 < jal0> do you see how the address lines are connected?
21:13 < antagonizt> the add* lines?
21:13 < jal0> yeap
21:13 < jal0> so the companion chip does not see the address the same way at the cpu
21:16 < jal0> so reading from say address xxxx xxxx xxx5, the companion may see xxxx xxxx xxxx xx1D
21:16 < jal0> but that just a guess, i have to figure out what the address lines on the companion chip are to be sure
21:18 < jal0> but what you can tell is that address xxx4,xxx8, and xxxC all reference the same memory location on the companion chip
21:19 < jal0> due to the fact that add4 and add3 are shorted
21:19 < jal0> is this making any sense to you ?
21:20 < antagonizt> not really...
21:20 < jal0> ;)
21:21 < jal0> you have any experience with microprocessor design?
21:21 < antagonizt> not on this high of a level... 
21:21 < jal0> that would explain it :). Once i know for sure what the conversion is i can start fixing the serial driver.
21:22 < antagonizt> i made a very simple mips processor about 2 years ago
21:22 < antagonizt> in altera
21:23 < antagonizt> the add pins are used to access memory?
21:24 < jal0> it actually very simple. just think of it in binary. if 0000 1000 is output on add1->add8, then due to the way add4 and add3 are shorted, the companion would see 0001 1100.
21:26 < jal0> whats altera
21:27 < antagonizt> vhdl design software
21:27 < jal0> yes add pins are for accessing memory
21:27 < jal0> data* for data
21:28 < jal0> at this level, the kernal sources dont help, you need to have the datasheets
21:29 < jal0> did you check out the link on the ASIC devices?
21:29 < jal0> that's what i believe the companion chip is
21:30 < antagonizt> cool
21:31 < jal0> now i just have to find which macro is used for the serial communications core, and things should start falling into place
21:32 < jal0> http://www.be-central.be/modules.php?op=modload&name=phpBB_14&file=index&action=viewtopic&topic=543&3
21:33 < jal0> for a bit on nestalgia(sp??)
21:55 < antagonizt> nostalgia
21:55 < jal0> ;)
